entries.title: Cinematic Scroll Choreography & Rhythm-Driven Layouts
entries.summary: Codrops' Podium case study reveals how scroll-driven motion choreography and narrative pacing can turn a portfolio into a cinematic experience — plus notes on Three.js morph target animation blending.

blocks.text:
**Highlighted Techniques (June 27, 2026)**

**1) Scroll-Driven Motion Choreography (Codrops — Podium)**
Podium treats scroll position as a film timeline: each viewport acts as a 'scene' with entrance/exit choreography timed to scroll velocity. Key techniques: CSS scroll-timeline for zero-JS trigger points, layered parallax with depth-aware opacity fade, and typographic rhythm that syncs font-weight transitions to scroll progress. The restraint principle — withholding animation until the user earns it through scrolling — creates anticipation and makes each reveal feel intentional.

**2) Morph Target Animation Blending (Three.js)**
Three.js examples demonstrate smooth blending between multiple morph targets using weighted interpolation, enabling organic shape transitions (e.g., facial expressions, fluid deformation). Combined with requestAnimationFrame pacing and easing curves, this creates lifelike animations without skeletal rigs — useful for hero sections with abstract 3D geometry that responds to cursor or scroll input.

entries.title: Daily Design Highlights: Three.js and More
entries.summary: Explored Three.js latest experiments to uncover a unique lighting technique and a cinematic particle system enhancement.

blocks.text:
**Highlighted Techniques (April 16, 2026)**

**1) Cinematic Particle System**
A Three.js experiment showcasing particle systems transformed using advanced GLSL shaders for depth and realism, integrated with scroll-based interactions.

**2) Unified Lighting with WebGPU**
The latest Three.js version simplifies WebGPU workflows, enabling seamless transitions and compatibility, offering developers flexibility when targeting high-performance browsers without complex setups.
